subject: Annotate facet_grid in panel coordinates instead of data coordinates?

messages.author: 40f327279f5af749
messages.subject: Annotate facet_grid in panel coordinates instead of data coordinates?
parts:
I am using facet_grid to create a 2D grid of scatter plots. Each plot
has a linear regression line. I'm annotating each panel with the
correlation coefficient. I'm using scales="free". I'd like to place
the annotations in a consistent location within each panel, e.g. the
upper left corner. In other words, I'd like to place the annotations
using the coordinates of the panel as opposed to the coordinates of
the data in the panel. Is there any way to do this?

For an example of the "problem," with the annotations placed in data
coordinates, please see:
http://gist.github.com/392102

Thanks,
AdamK

messages.subject: RE: Annotate facet_grid in panel coordinates instead of data coordinates?
parts:
Hadley,

Thanks for the super quick response!

In follow up to your suggestion: I assume you mean to use ddply and range to calculate the min and max for the data in each row and column of panels? This would work up to a point, but if I'm including a geom_smooth(method="lm", fullrange=TRUE, se=TRUE), then the band around the fit line may extend beyond the data range, which in turn will change the range of the facets. Is there a way to query the plot itself about what the range will be for each facet, so that the code doesn't have to know what particular data will be displayed?

Thanks,
AdamK

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: Annotate facet_grid in panel coordinates instead of data  coordinates?
parts:
This might work for you,

set.seed(123)
d= data.frame(x=rnorm(40), y=rnorm(40), f1=rep(1:2, each=20), f2=
sample(letters[1:2], 40, rep=T))
p = ggplot(d) + geom_path(aes(x,y)) + facet_grid(f1~f2, scales="free")
p + geom_text(aes(x,y,label=x),data=data.frame(x=rep(-Inf, 4),
y=rep(Inf,4), f1=rep(1:2,each=2), f2=rep(letters[1:2],2)), vjust=1,
hjust=0)


HTH,

baptiste

messages.subject: Re: Annotate facet_grid in panel coordinates instead of data  coordinates?
parts:
Thank you Baptiste! This does exactly what I want.

In case anyone missed it in the details of the code: Using Inf and -
Inf for the x or y coordinates allows one to refer to the left,
right, top, and bottom of each panel.

Apparently this is a new feature as of ggplot2 version 0.8.5. Thanks
to Hadley for adding this.

adamk

messages.subject: Re: Annotate facet_grid in panel coordinates instead of data  coordinates?
parts:
I'd like to bring this up again as I was looking for this for the same
thing and generally Baptiste's solution works great. However in my
case I also have margins=T and have run into an additional issue.
Using his example above with two changes: setting margins=T for
facets_grid, and putting different values for the 'x' label variable
so as to illustrate the issue (instead of -Inf).

f2=sample(letters[1:2], 40, rep=T))

p = ggplot(d) + geom_path(aes(x,y)) + facet_grid(f1~f2, scales="free",
margins=T)

p + geom_text(aes(x,y,label=x),data=data.frame(x=1:4,

As one can see, in the margin cells, the previous cell labels are
posted again (and in my own graph they are simply being written on top
of one another as I set the x and y to specific values in aes). I
tried making that data.frame constructed in the geom_text part such
that both factors would actually have an (all) category in them with
the hopes that I could manually label the (all) cells, but
unfortunately that just shifted the cells with problem to the next
cell in the graph (e.g. in the graph produced above, I could get that
first row third cell the way I wanted but the '1 2' cell would then
shift to the leftmost cell in the next row, and all subsequent cell
labels would be shifted accordingly). If anyone has any thoughts it'd
be much appreciated, even for just not displaying anything at all in
the margin cells. However in my case I'm trying to display cell
sample sizes for each plot and so being able to label the margin plots
would be nice also.

Other than that I've been using ggplot2 for a couple weeks now and
would like to say thanks for the great package.
